title: Ik ben, jij bent — voornaamwoorden en zijn
summary: All the personal pronouns, the verb zijn (to be), and the je-vs-u register

blocks.title: The people words
blocks.body: Every sentence needs a subject. Here's the full set. Note that Dutch has **two** words in three slots: *jij/je*, *hij* pairs with *zij/ze* for 'she', and *zij/ze* also means 'they'. The short forms (*je, ze, we*) are what you actually hear — the long forms (*jij, zij, wij*) add stress.
blocks.callout: *zij/ze* pulls double duty: 'she' and 'they'. The verb tells you which.

blocks.title: The verb zijn (to be)
blocks.body: *zijn* is the most-used verb in Dutch, and — like 'to be' in English — it's irregular, so you memorise it. Learn this table cold; everything leans on it.
blocks.callout: Three shapes only: *ben, bent, is, zijn*. Plurals all take *zijn*.

blocks.prompt: Fill the gap: Hij ___ mijn vriend. (He is my friend.)
blocks.explain: *hij* (he) takes *is*. *ben* is only for *ik*; *bent* is for *jij/u*.
*Ik ben.* This one form you'll say more than any other.
*Wij zijn hier* — we are here. Plural subjects all take *zijn*.

blocks.title: je or u? — the register switch
blocks.body: This is the choice you make every time you talk to someone new. **je** is warm and casual: friends, family, kids, colleagues you know. **u** is polite and respectful: strangers, older people, officials, the doctor, a shopkeeper you don't know. Guess wrong toward *u* and you're just a bit formal — harmless. Guess wrong toward *je* with the wrong person and it can feel too familiar.
blocks.callout: When in doubt, start with *u*. People will often say *"je mag je zeggen"* — 'you can use je' — and then you switch.

pairs.note: 'What's your name?' — *je* to a new colleague at a party, *u* to the person at the town-hall desk.
With *u* the verb also shifts to *wilt*. Register changes the whole sentence, not just the pronoun.

blocks.scene: A borrel at Emma's. She introduces you to the room.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Iedereen, dit is mijn vriend. Hij leert Nederlands!
lines.en: Everyone, this is my friend. He's learning Dutch!
lines.spotlight: *dit is* = this is — *is*, the hij/zij/het form of zijn.

blocks.prompt: Write three 'I am / you are / we are' sentences about real people — a friend, yourself, your group. Use *ben*, *bent* and *zijn* once each.
